reviews.title: Too long sign up and too complicated
reviews.text: First the app asks you to create a user id.  It wants an email address and if you click continue as guest it allows you to go on a long chain of entering info then circles back to the point where you have to access it through an account or email address, so there is no way to just download and use it.  Second, that long chain of info it asks for? Well, it wants your interests, your age, and everything else under the sun.  For an app that is supposed to help you defeat bias, it sets you up for BIAS right from the door by setting an algorithm to target information toward you. I don’t even complete the process before I canceled the free 7 day.  Canceled as soon as I reached the sign in page requiring me to sign in by creating an account AFTER I already chose continue as guest because I was so irritated that the app was asking for all kinds of information up to that point, that I lost trust in it when it circled back to asking me to create an account after I already basically said no in my selection to use it as a guest.

reviews.title: In the name of providing “balanced” coverage, it includes right wing information that’s not true.
reviews.text:
I have used this app for about a year and a half. However, every time I read a story, a news piece, it adds in things like “what the left misses.”, and what the “what the right misses”, for each posted story. The problem with this is that it struggles to find information that the left doesn’t cover, that makes them look bad, because they don’t talk about things like financial impacts, that Republicans use as arguments to make their case about volatile subjects. However, in reverse, they failed to acknowledge that right wing news outlets don’t just not cover the angle of left politics, but they also make it look as if left-wing people are the uninformed, making it look like left-wing persons are the ones trying to jack around the media response to our world.. It’s the same way where NPR will have “both sides” in an interview, where you have to listen to someone who is clearly a right wing zealot. That’s not balance. That’s reciprocation to power..

I cannot recommend this app any longer. It’s not because I don’t want to know what the “other half” knows. We, the left, ALREADY know. It’s the right, that doesn’t know what’s going on. And being gaslit, the left, like we aren’t aware, makes this app seem very weirdly pro right at the end of the day. Pick your own new sources. Be smart. Know you’re biases and blind spots. Ask your friends and other people you don’t know about their opinions about things. You do not need it to be put in front of you to consume, to be a good person in

reviews.title: Doesn’t obey your Adblocker settings - GET SPAMMED!
reviews.text:
TLDR; use the browser, not this app, to view ground News, and you’ll be much happier. 
For the Devs: thanks for the response! I want to love it. I do. But the until you can use my preferred browser (Firefox on iOS at the moment) to open news articles, or until your existing newsreader can properly block ads, the app is a very poor reading experience after the second click. I get that you’re obeying apples Safari position, but they now allow a different browser to be designated the system default. All you’d have to do is allow for the new  “open in default browser” and I could give you five stars. 

I love the Ground News service, and read regularly via my browser over a vpn. However, The iOS dedicated Ground News App is inferior in simply every measure-able way versus browsing the site online. The app tries to actively annoy you into paid feature, and still delivers a subpar UX. See below. 

1. The app exposes more personal data than a properly anonymized browser session in chrome or Firefox would give up. 

2. This matters, it turns out, because the ground News app also doesn’t honor any of your Adblock or cookie settings. Yes, that’s right: it’s like the web from 2004 all over again, with pop ups, popovers, popunders, please confirm our cookie policy, our privacy policy, would you like to subscribe? and little floating ads simply plastering the page. Just.no. Using the app causes something like 40-60% of your screen to be covered by ads! But use Firefox with adguard to view

reviews.title: Not neutral at all, leans left in many ways
reviews.text:
For a platform that advertises itself as basically a neutral arbiter of news, this app falls WAY, short of that. I’ve been doing a three month analysis of the “summaries“ of the major stories every single day, and… They always have a left-wing bias. It is a little gentle, not obtuse and super obvious like Apple news/yahoo/Google/BBC/NBC/MSNBC/CNN, etc., but it is absolutely there, and it is constant. I recommended this app to several people who subscribed, and then I had to apologize to them because I don’t feel like I can endorse it. I know I’m not alone in this complaint.
Just don’t say you’re neutral, unless you’re going to be. And just because you offer things like “Blindspot“ and “the breakdown of which political size of the aisle put out/published certain stories“ doesn’t mean that you’re offering the product that you essentially claim to offer. You don’t. And it’s sort of seems to me like a Trojan horse operation in that way. So there you go that’s my two cents.

reviews.title: Sign in with Apple Account on MacOS Not Working
reviews.text: iOS app works as expected. MacOS accepts TouchID then just remains on the screen and never actually logs in. Signing in as a Guest shows the private relay and says that I have a subscription but it remains on the free (which makes sense since that was the “Guest login”). Not sure what the issue is but it is disappointing.

reviews.title: The Middle Ground Isn’t Always the Best
reviews.text:
If I have to read the phrase “reflects a deep ideological divide” at the end of an ‘analysis’ with zero understanding of context, I might go mad. 

Beyond the poor AI summaries and coverage of bias, it reflects a dangerously unacknowledged assumption that the median between left and right is most factual. It’s intellectually lazy and I feel an average reader will come away thinking they’re better informed and more ‘balanced’ on the issue, when instead they’ve taken misleading framing as half-right rather than outright deception.
